summary: Following the total annihilation of Edgeshade by an apocalyptic swarm of awakened dragons—an event for which Waluigi officially accepts zero legal liability despite his documented presence holding a stolen Gold Dragon egg—Archie Miser and Markop navigated the deeply hostile outskirts of the Midlands. They eventually converged on the mist-shrouded, faction-torn town of Ravencreek, and later, the towering aerodrome of Swiftsoul Keep. This arc, spanning several grueling weeks of Efferd 1040 BF, was defined by an intricate web of factional politics, underworld assassinations, bureaucratic fraud, and catastrophic magical evolution. First, there was the party's deepening entanglement with the mysterious Rakasha, Rakka, whose demands fractured the group's tactical cohesion, forcing Markop to remain behind and unexpectedly master the volatile, highly dangerous art of Goblin Alchemy. Second, there was the unsupervised town exploration of Archie Miser, which alienated nearly every major faction in Ravencreek and culminated in an intellectually bankrupt assassination attempt via a heated sauna organized by a Toad with a suitcase. Third, there was the terrifying theological evolution of the nameless Toad whom Archie had casually abandoned in the burning ruins of Edgeshade. This Toad, having stumbled upon a fully intact Crystal Star shard, ascended to become the 'God Toad,' initiating a cult of vengeance fueled by petty grievances and cosmic power. Fourth, the chaotic convergence of the entire future 'Disaster Inc.' roster occurred at Swiftsoul Keep. This involved a fraudulent gladiator match featuring a man in a papier-mâché dragon suit named Gary, an enraged Bowser crashing the ring out of sheer professional offense, and Wario faking his own death in an elaborate scheme involving a discarded syringe, a damaged clockwork hand, and a funeral guest list. Waluigi is documenting this sequence with exhaustive, excruciating detail because it represents the exact period during which the party transitioned from 'clumsy vagabonds' to 'international fugitives and alleged mass murderers.' The arc concluded with the Swiftsoul Keep trial, presided over by Miles Edgeworth, and the party's desperate departure aboard the stolen military airship 'Vigilance,' leaving their pirate allies behind on the docks. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting this arc with particular focus on the logistical gaps, the psychological deterioration of the participants, the intricate factional standing systems of the Midlands, and the sheer volume of unforced errors that characterized the party's movements. To achieve a comprehensive understanding of the 1040 BF crisis, one must dissect the transition from Ravencreek to Swiftsoul. It involves weeks of missing time, highly questionable decision-making, groundbreaking alchemical discoveries, the exploitation of bureaucratic loopholes, and the specific, bloody circumstances of how the core group of Disaster Inc. finally assembled into a single, cohesive unit of mass destruction.

To understand the gravity of these events, one must first understand the state of the Midlands in Efferd of 1040 BF. The sky was no longer a safe ceiling; it was a contested zone filled with millions of displaced dragons. The economy had collapsed into bartering, paranoia, and opportunistic banditry. The political landscape was a razor's edge defined by complex reputation thresholds. The Vampires of Fairth's Retreat, the Frostclaw Werewolves, the Knights Guild, the Archers Guild, the Wizards Guild, the Thieves, the Nobles, and the Regal Empire were all operating on a hair-trigger. A single misstep could plunge a traveler's status from 'Neutral' to 'Hunted' or 'Mortal Enemy.' And walking blindly through the middle of this societal breakdown were a young fighter desperately searching for his captured father, a young mage whose relationship with fire safety was notoriously flexible, and a crew of pirates who had decided that following these two teenagers was somehow a better career choice than maritime crime.

## Part I: Bureaucratic Fraud and the Nature of Magic


Before delving into the events of Ravencreek, Waluigi must establish the administrative context in which certain individuals were operating during this period. The Midlands, despite being a fractured and collapsing territory, still maintained a rigid, albeit deeply flawed, bureaucratic registry for adventurers, mercenaries, and magic users. The way individuals were classified determined their access to cities, their treatment by local authorities, and their legal standing.

Waluigi has managed to procure the official registration documents filed with the Regal Empire's regional administration for two specific individuals involved in this crisis: Wario and himself. Waluigi presents these documents here to illustrate the profound, systemic failure of Midlands intelligence gathering.

Behold the official, legally binding description of Wario, as approved by a presumably blind, deaf, and heavily concussed clerk:

> *'Wario is a formidable warrior who swears allegiance to rulers, religious orders, and noble causes. Wario's alignment dictates the degree to which he upholds his pledges. Whether embarking on a quest or safeguarding a realm, Wario typically journeys with a retinue that includes squires and hirelings who are commoners.'*

Waluigi requires the reader to pause and let the sheer, unadulterated audacity of that paragraph wash over them. 

Wario. The man who stole Gold Dragon eggs to sell to the Nocturnaether Conclave. The man who faked his own death to avoid paying his debts. The man who shoulder-barged Markop during an art auction to steal a book. This man successfully registered himself as a *Paladin*. 

He claimed to swear allegiance to 'rulers, religious orders, and noble causes.' Wario's only allegiance is to the gravitational pull of gold coins. His 'alignment' does indeed dictate the degree to which he upholds his pledges, and that alignment is 'Aggressive Capitalism.' The 'squires and hirelings' mentioned in his official retinue were not devoted followers; they were terrified local commoners whom Wario had bullied into carrying his luggage and setting up his campsite, individuals he routinely abandoned the moment a situation required actual combat. 

The fact that Wario used this 'noble warrior' classification to bypass checkpoints, commandeer supplies, and demand diplomatic immunity while actively orchestrating the Swiftsoul Keep explosion is a testament to his sociopathic genius. It is also proof that the Regal Empire's background check protocols consisted entirely of asking, 'Are you a good guy?' and accepting 'WAHAHA, YES!' as a legally binding affidavit.

Conversely, let us examine Waluigi's own official registry entry, which Waluigi considers a rare moment of bureaucratic accuracy:

> *'Mages spend their lives delving into the arcane mysteries, and Waluigi is no exception. Unlike other mages who may advise nobles or conduct isolated experiments, Waluigi's magical prowess is often overshadowed by his mischievous nature. He thrives on creating chaos and mischief through his magical abilities.'*

Waluigi stands by every word of this. It is elegant. It is true. Waluigi does not hide behind false declarations of nobility. Waluigi is a scholar of the arcane who recognizes that true mastery of magic requires testing its boundaries, often by applying it to situations where it does not belong. Chaos is not an accident for Waluigi; it is an artistic medium. 

The distinction is critical. Wario creates chaos because he is greedy and lacks foresight. Archie Miser creates chaos because he is clumsy and untrained. Waluigi creates chaos because the universe is rigid, boring, and structurally offensive, and applying a precisely calculated amount of mischief is the only way to make it interesting. Waluigi is a professional. Everyone else is an amateur playing with matches.

## Part II:


The Outskirts — Rakka's House and the Tactics of Separation

The ash of Edgeshade was still clinging to their boots when Archie Miser and Markop, flanked by the remnants of Captain Sugar's pirate crew, reached the gloomy, weeping outskirts of the Ravencreek region. The landscape here is unforgiving—a perpetually damp, twilight-drenched expanse of sinking mud, twisted roots, and shadows that seem to move independently of the light. They were actively pursuing the trail of Markop's captured father, who had been snatched in the dragon-induced chaos of the festival.

Their pursuit led them to an anomalous structure that defied local geometry. It was a house that seemed to occupy slightly more space on the inside than the exterior dimensions would allow. It smelled of old incense, damp earth, and secrets.

This was the residence of Rakka, the Rakasha.

Rakka, a planar observer and information broker, held the intelligence Markop desperately needed: his father's captors had headed toward Swiftsoul Keep. But Rakka did not dispense information out of altruism. Rakka traded in favors, obligations, and labor. She presented a two-pronged demand to the party.

First, Markop was tasked with staying behind to guard her house. Second, Archie Miser was dispatched on an 'ingredient quest' into the town of Ravencreek to gather specific, highly volatile components.

Waluigi notes this as a masterclass in operational manipulation. By separating them, Rakka neutralized the group's most reliable combatant and sent its most volatile liability into a densely populated, politically unstable town unsupervised. Archie, without Markop to anchor him, is a thermodynamic disaster waiting for an excuse. Markop, without Archie to protect, becomes a static asset. Rakka engineered this separation perfectly, ensuring she had a capable guard while someone else took the physical risk of navigating the town's underworld.

Markop agreed. He agreed because he is a soldier at heart, and when a powerful entity offers you the coordinates of your kidnapped father in exchange for standing at a door, you stand at the door. Archie, accompanied by the bewildered and heavily unwashed pirates, took the ingredient list and headed toward the fog-choked streets of Ravencreek.

## Part III:


The Science of Goblin Alchemy

While Archie bumbled into town, Markop remained at the house. However, Markop did not merely stand guard. Recognizing the escalating threat level of their environment, and recalling the bizarre dancing goblins they had witnessed on the slopes of Dragon Mountain (a manifestation of extreme ambient fey magic leaking from the mountain's subterranean depths), Markop entered into a period of intensive, albeit highly dangerous, scholastic study under Rakka's peripheral guidance.

Markop is not a mage. Markop is a physical combatant. But survival in the Midlands requires adaptation. During his tenure guarding Rakka's domicile, Markop spent his time mastering the esoteric, highly volatile discipline of Goblin Alchemy.

Goblin Alchemy is not the refined, sterile science of the Mages' Guild. It does not use measured beakers, pure reagents, or peer-reviewed magical theory. It is a chaotic, instinctive process of mashing toxic flora, monster glands, and raw, unfiltered fey energy together until it stops smoking and starts glowing. It is dangerous to the brewer, dangerous to the consumer, and absolutely devastating to the enemy.

Waluigi has managed to procure Markop's field notes from this period, which read less like a textbook and more like a recipe book for catastrophic side effects. Markop successfully synthesized eight distinct concoctions, utilizing the ambient fey magic and bizarre flora of the Ravencreek outskirts. Waluigi will document them here, as they became crucial to the party's survival in subsequent engagements:

**1. Goblim Brew Elix: Kruglom Zizzl Grog**
> *'A myst'rious green pot'n that, when quaff'd, grants the drink'r temp'rary enhanc'd speed an' agil'ty, mimickin' goblin-like quickness.'*
Waluigi notes that the tactical advantage of doubled movement speed in combat is undeniable. However, the side effects of 'Kruglom Zizzl Grog' often include severe gastrointestinal distress, hyperventilation, and a temporary inability to speak in anything other than high-pitched, manic shrieks. Markop would later use this to outflank heavily armored opponents, terrifying them not just with his speed, but with the unholy noises he produced while moving.

**2. Grog of Invisibl'ty: Snikkleshroud Mizzle**
> *'A cloudy concoct'n that turns the imbiber invisibl' fer a short durat'n, perfect fer sneaky goblin tactics.'*
Markop's synthesis of the Snikkleshroud Mizzle was reportedly unstable. While it effectively bent light around the user, rendering them invisible to the naked eye, the chemical reaction caused the user's pores to emit a profound, inescapable smell of wet cabbage and sulfur. This rendered the 'sneaky' aspect somewhat moot against creatures with functional olfactory senses, such as the local Frostclaw werewolf packs. It was invisibility for the eyes, but a beacon for the nose.

**3. Goblinkfire Ess'nce: Blazefizz Gloomvial**
> *'A vial containin' a fiery liquid that, when hurl'd, creates a small explos'n of green flames, causin' damage to enemies.'*
This was Markop's primary artillery development. The Blazefizz Gloomvial is not normal fire. It burns with a magical resonance that adheres to flesh, armor, and even stone. It consumes oxygen at an alarming rate and emits a blinding green flash upon detonation. Markop transformed himself from a purely melee fighter into a tactical grenadier with this invention, deploying it with a ruthless, calculated efficiency that Archie Miser's wild fireballs severely lacked.

**4. Goblin's Gambit Tonic: Mischifflask Wilybrew**
> *'A bubbly pot'n that grants the drink'r a temp'rary boost to luck an' cunnin', increasin' the chances of successful thievin' or trick'ry.'*
Waluigi frankly resents the existence of a potion that mimics his own natural, magnificent cunning. To distill the essence of mischief into a bottle is an insult to the art form. However, Waluigi acknowledges its utility for someone as historically straightforward as Markop. When Markop needed to lie, cheat, or manipulate a locked mechanism, the Wilybrew smoothed out his honest edges and replaced them with temporary sociopathy.

**5. Mischief Mend'r Pot'n: Glimmertide Healbrew**
> *'A healin' elixir infus'd with goblin magic, it rest'res a mod'rate amount of health an' leaves a mischievous, fleetin' glow 'round the heal'd area.'*
Goblin healing is rarely painless. The Glimmertide Healbrew forces cellular regeneration at a terrifying speed, knitting wounds together with an aggressive, stinging sensation. The most notable side effect is the 'fleetin' glow.' The healed tissue bioluminesces for several hours. This is tactically disastrous in stealth operations, turning the healed subject into a glowing green target in the dark. But beggars cannot be choosers in the Midlands wilderness, and a glowing arm is preferable to a severed one.

**6. Sticky Fing'rs Syrup: Tanglegrasp Glooz**
> *'A viscous substance that, when appli'd to hands or objects, enhanc's dexterity an' pickpocketin' skills for a short period.'*
A highly specialized adhesive that reacts to the user's intent. When applied to the fingertips, it allows for the manipulation of delicate mechanisms, the silent removal of objects from pockets, and the ability to scale sheer surfaces for brief periods. It smells strongly of pine tar and regret.

**7. Goblin Gaseous Grenade: Puffbane Goblinbomb**
> *'A small glass globe fill'd with a noxious gas that, when shatter'd, creates a cloud of disorientin' fumes, providin' a quick escape or diversion.'*
The Puffbane Goblinbomb is chemical warfare in a jar. The gas it releases is a concentrated aerosol of hallucinogens and irritants. Those caught in the blast radius experience immediate tearing of the eyes, violent coughing fits, and a profound sense of existential dread. Markop used these specifically for crowd control and to break line-of-sight against superior numbers.

**8. Sneaky Sneak Serum: Whispershade Draught**
> *'A pot'n that temp'rar'ly grants the ability to move silently, makin' the us'r nearly undetectable while sneakin'.'*
Unlike the Snikkleshroud Mizzle, this draught does not bend light; it absorbs sound. The user's footsteps, breathing, and even the rustling of their armor are magically muted. It is the pinnacle of Markop's alchemical studies during this period, allowing a heavily armored centaur to move with the silence of a falling leaf.

Markop transformed himself during this period. While he was carefully measuring Blazefizz Gloomvials and calculating the explosive yield of Puffbane Goblinbombs, his companion was busy dismantling their diplomatic standing in the neighboring town with the efficiency of a wrecking ball in a glassware shop.

## Part IV: Archie's Unsupervised Town Exploration and Factional Disaster


Ravencreek in 1040 BF was a geopolitical powder keg. The town sat in a valley enveloped by perpetual, clinging mist, serving as the tense borderland between territories controlled by the Frostclaw werewolf packs (who dominated the surrounding forests) and the aristocratic vampire covens of Fairth's Retreat (who maintained several 'neutral' establishments within the town limits). 

The streets were cobbled, narrow, and slick with moisture. The locals operated on a strict, unspoken code of conduct. You did not ask questions. You did not look too closely at the cargo being unloaded at midnight. You respected the delicate balance of power. According to the official Regal Empire sociometric registry, a traveler's reputation status in such a town was paramount; it could range from an 'Esteemed' ally to an 'Eternal Enemy' Pariah, and that status determined whether you were served a drink or served to the local wildlife.

Archie Miser, accompanied by the loudly swearing, aggressively unwashed remnants of Captain Sugar's pirate crew, entered Ravencreek with Rakka's ingredient list and absolutely zero diplomatic tact. 

Waluigi must emphasize that when Waluigi enters a hostile town, he does so with grace. He assesses the power structures. He identifies the marks. He applies charm, bribery, or intimidation with surgical precision. Archie, conversely, creates chaos not as an art form, but entirely by accident. Archie is a bull in a china shop who believes he is a ballet dancer.

Archie's methodology for acquiring the highly illegal, deeply suspicious magical components on Rakka's list was brutally abrasive. He lacked the subtlety required for underworld negotiations. He walked into apothecaries, components shops, and shady taverns, loudly demanding restricted items and arguing with the proprietors when they feigned ignorance.

The resulting factional fallout was mathematically disastrous. Waluigi has modeled the reputation shifts based on Archie's reported behavior throughout the afternoon:

*   **ShopKeepers Faction:** Dropped from 'Neutral' (Threshold 5) to 'Banned' (Threshold -40). Archie aggressively haggled for items he did not understand, demanding discounts on rare graveyard dirt. When a merchant refused, Archie accidentally produced a minor thermal surge, setting fire to a display of highly flammable dried mandrake root. He then insulted the merchant's lineage while being chased out with a broom.
*   **Thieves Faction:** Dropped from 'Ignored' (Threshold 10) to 'Watched' (Threshold -10), and rapidly approached 'Targeted' (Threshold -30). The pirates accompanying Archie, lacking any sense of operational security, loudly boasted in a local tavern about their stolen loot from the burning of Edgeshade. This drew the immediate ire of the local, organized Thieves Guild, who deeply resented unauthorized, untaxed freelance crime occurring in their territory. The local cutpurses began marking Archie and the pirates for acquisition.
*   **Townsfolk Faction:** Plummeted from 'Neutral' (Threshold 10) directly to 'Disliked' (Threshold -10). The presence of heavily armed, soot-stained teenagers and loudly swearing pirates singing sea shanties in landlocked, quiet taverns deeply disturbed the civilian populace. Mothers pulled their children inside. Doors were locked. The general consensus was that Archie brought the stench of disaster with him.
*   **Guards Faction:** Shifted dangerously from 'Neutral' (Threshold 5) to 'Untrusted' (Threshold -5). The Ravencreek constabulary—already stretched thin managing the vampire/werewolf tensions—began actively shadowing the group. They recognized Archie as a high-risk variable in a town already balancing on a knife-edge. Every move he made was logged by suspicious watchmen.

In the span of four hours, Archie had systematically burned every bridge in town, blissfully unaware of the complex sociopolitical thresholds he was violating. He treated a delicate ecosystem of predators and prey like a shopping mall. 

And because he was making so much noise, because his magical signature was flaring with unfiltered anxiety, he attracted the attention of the absolute worst faction currently operating in the shadows of the Midlands.

## Part V:


The Veilwood Spa Assassination Attempt — A Case Study in Thermodynamic Incompetence

While Archie blundered through the markets, entirely oblivious to the hostile glares of the local constabulary and the thieves guild, he was approached by a Toad. 

This Toad was dressed in a pristine, perfectly tailored, pinstriped suit—a jarring, almost hallucinatory contrast to the mud, fog, and squalor of Ravencreek. He carried a leather suitcase. His posture was rigid. His smile was wide, fixed, and entirely devoid of warmth. It was the smile of an entity performing the concept of a smile based on written instructions.

Waluigi has since identified this individual as a high-ranking acolyte—perhaps one of the first true zealots—of the newly formed Cult of the God Toad. The cult was spreading rapidly through the subterranean networks and displaced populations of the Midlands, recruiting disgruntled, overlooked Toads and offering them a doctrine of cosmic revenge. They had tracked Archie—known in their nascent scripture as 'The Betrayer'—to Ravencreek.

The Suitcase Toad approached Archie with a proposition. He recognized Archie and the pirates as 'weary travelers' who had clearly endured the horrific hardships of the recent dragon attacks. With a voice like oiled glass, he offered them an exclusive, complimentary relaxation session at the Veilwood Spa.

The Veilwood Spa was a luxury establishment on the elevated edge of town. It was known to the underworld as a strict neutral zone, owned and operated by aristocratic vampires affiliated with Fairth's Retreat. It catered to the wealthy, the powerful, and those who needed to conduct business without fear of assassination.

Archie, whose critical thinking skills are frequently, tragically overridden by the promise of free amenities and a hot bath, accepted without hesitation. The pirates, who had not seen soap since before Edgeshade burned, eagerly agreed. They followed the Suitcase Toad through the winding streets.

The exterior of the Veilwood Spa was magnificent—dark, polished mahogany, intricate stained glass depicting nocturnal scenes, and the faint, coppery smell of eucalyptus masking the underlying, ever-present scent of ancient blood. The Suitcase Toad led them past the pale, unblinking vampire receptionists—who watched them with predatory disinterest—down a series of winding, steam-filled, marble-tiled corridors, and deep into the facility's subterranean levels.

They arrived at a specialized thermal chamber. A sauna.

The Suitcase Toad provided them with thick, plush towels. He gestured politely for them to step inside the wooden room. 

Archie and the pirates stepped in. 

The Suitcase Toad smiled his terrible, fixed smile. 'The master sends his regards,' he said, his voice dropping the veneer of hospitality.

He then slammed the heavy, iron-reinforced oak door shut. The lock clicked with the heavy, definitive, unmistakable sound of a vault sealing. Immediately, hidden vents in the floor hissed to life, pumping thick, scalding steam into the small room. The temperature skyrocketed in seconds.

Waluigi must now spend a considerable amount of text analyzing the sheer, mind-boggling, intellectually bankrupt incompetence of this assassination attempt.

The God Toad's cult had successfully lured their primary target into an isolated, soundproof, highly secure room. They had him locked in. They had the element of surprise. 

And what kind of room did they choose to trap a highly volatile, completely untrained, panic-prone *Fire Evocation Mage* inside? 

A room entirely constructed of dry wood, specifically designed to get incredibly hot.

If the cult's intent was to kill Archie via heat exhaustion, suffocation, or boiling steam, they fundamentally misunderstood the nature of the man they were fighting. Archie Miser does not die of heat; Archie Miser *causes* heat. His magical core is attuned to thermal energy. The sauna trap was not a death sentence for Archie; it was an incubator. It was a loaded gun handed to a pyromaniac.

Furthermore, this action constituted a gross violation of the delicate political balance of the Midlands. By attempting to murder someone inside the Veilwood Spa, the God Toad's cult had inadvertently deployed what Waluigi later heard described in intercepted communications as 'Anti-Vampire Tactics.' As one Onyx Hand operative noted in a leaked internal memo regarding the incident: *'Anti-Vampire Tactics within a designated neutral zone... I smell a Hate Crime.'* 

The vampires of Fairth's Retreat did not appreciate their expensive, neutral-ground establishment being used as an execution chamber by upstart toad cultists. Archie's eventual fiery response would severely damage his and his associates' relations with the Vampire faction, pushing his status dangerously toward 'Enemy' (Threshold -20).

Inside the sauna, the pirates began to panic. They threw their considerable weight against the iron-banded door, quickly discovering that pirate muscle, fueled by rum and scurvy, is largely ineffective against vampire-grade reinforced oak. The air grew stifling. 

Archie, realizing he had been outmaneuvered by a Toad with a suitcase and a creepy smile, began charging a massive fireball. He drew the ambient heat of the sauna into his core, his hands glowing with unstable, destructive intent. He was fully prepared to blow the door off its hinges, likely taking down half the spa's structural supports, incinerating several innocent vampire masseuses, and bringing the entire building down on their heads in the process.

But Archie did not have to cast the spell.

Back at Rakka's house on the outskirts of town, Markop had experienced a tactical revelation. Whether Rakka had officially dismissed him from his guard duty upon receiving the necessary scrying information, or whether Markop's survival instincts simply screamed that leaving Archie alone in a hostile town for more than three hours was a statistical guarantee of utter disaster, Markop abandoned his post.

Armed with his newly synthesized arsenal of Goblin Alchemy—specifically a bandolier of Blazefizz Gloomvials, several Puffbane Goblinbombs, and a flask of Kruglom Zizzl Grog—he sprinted the entire distance from the outskirts into the heart of Ravencreek.

Markop is a seasoned tracker. He did not wander aimlessly. He tracked them through the town using footprint analysis in the mud, noting the agitated reactions of the townsfolk, and simply following the general aura of impending catastrophe that always trailed Archie. He arrived at the Veilwood Spa.

He did not announce himself. He bypassed the vampire receptionists by simply not stopping to speak to them, moving with the heavy, armored momentum of a centaur on a mission. He navigated the steam-filled corridors, following the sound of pirates screaming and the rising hum of Archie charging a fireball.

He found the locked sauna door.

Markop did not attempt to pick the lock. He did not search for the Suitcase Toad to demand the key. Markop is a fighter who has recently embraced the explosive potential of goblin science. He views locked doors not as obstacles, but as targets.

Drawing a Blazefizz Gloomvial, Markop smashed it directly against the iron locking mechanism. The green goblin-fire erupted with a concentrated, localized concussive blast that superheated and shattered the iron. Before the metal could cool, Markop delivered a single, devastating kinetic strike with his hind hooves. 

The iron-banded oak door shattered inward, exploding into a shower of splinters and burning green residue. A massive cloud of superheated steam billowed out into the corridor, followed by a pile of coughing, half-boiled pirates and a very angry, heavily glowing Archie Miser.

The party was reunited. The sauna trap had been violently dismantled. But the words of the Suitcase Toad hung in the heavy, eucalyptus-scented air: *'The master sends his regards.'* 

They now knew they were being actively hunted by an organized force. And the trajectory of the hunt was pointing inexorably toward the highest, most prominent point in the town.

## Part VI:


The Ascension of the God Toad and the Siege of the Mayor's Manor

The town of Ravencreek was officially governed by a Mayor, a minor noble who resided in a sprawling, gothic manor perched atop a steep hill overlooking the misty streets. Or, at least, it *had* been governed by the Mayor.

By the time Archie, Markop, and the soot-stained pirates marched up the winding cobblestone path toward the estate, the Mayor was no longer in charge, and was likely no longer alive. The manor had been seized in a rapid, violent coup. The God Toad had taken up residence, utilizing the grand estate's elevated position and magical leylines as the focal point for his ritual of absolute divine ascension.

Waluigi must pause to explicitly explain the God Toad's origins, because they represent the exact kind of karmic, cosmic backlash that Waluigi deeply appreciates when it happens to someone other than himself. 

During the night Edgeshade burned, amid the absolute chaos of the apocalyptic dragon attack, Archie Miser had been traveling with a nameless, generic Toad carrying a simple wooden staff. When the situation became dire, when the flames closed in and survival required speed, Archie turned to this Toad, looked him in the eye, and said, 'Wait here, I'll be back.'

Archie lied. Archie fled the town and absolutely, unconditionally, never looked back.

That nameless Toad obeyed. He waited in the ashes. He waited as the dragons roared overhead, incinerating everything he knew. He waited as the buildings collapsed and the heat blistered his skin. And as he waited, realizing he had been abandoned to die by a supposed 'hero,' the sky above the ruins split open.

A fully formed, brilliant, reality-warping shard of a Crystal Star—one of the most potent artifacts in the cosmos—plummeted from the heavens and landed directly at his feet.

The Toad picked it up.

When a mortal mind interfaces with an artifact of limitless cosmic potential, the result is heavily dependent on the mortal's psychological state at the moment of contact. This Toad was utterly consumed by feelings of abandonment, betrayal, terror, and absolute, pristine pettiness. The Crystal Star did not heal him; it magnified his trauma by a factor of infinity. 

The Toad did not just gain magical power; he gained a divine complex fueled by grievance. He became the God Toad. And his entire theological foundation, his very reason for godhood, was based on the premise that Archie Miser was a treacherous monster who needed to be punished with cosmic severity.

As the party approached the iron gates of the Mayor's Manor, the reality-warping effects of the God Toad's presence became aggressively, viscerally obvious.

The grand stone fountains in the manor's sprawling courtyard were no longer spraying clear mountain water. They were actively pumping thick, viscous, bubbling crimson blood.

Waluigi has read the municipal damage reports filed by Ravencreek's surviving sanitation department months after the incident. The God Toad's erratic, vengeance-fueled magic had fundamentally corrupted the local water table. Every pipe, every aqueduct, every well, and every decorative birdbath connected to the manor's plumbing infrastructure had been transmuted into a grotesque cardiovascular system. The smell was overpowering—a heavy, hot, metallic stench of iron and salt that made the pirates gag, caused Markop's horse-instincts to panic, and drove the local vampire population in the town below into a state of highly agitated, frenzied confusion.

The party did not knock. Markop, heavily utilizing the momentum of his goblin potions, kicked open the front doors of the manor, shattering the hinges.

What followed was a brutal, room-by-room siege against a fanatical enemy. The manor was defended by the God Toad's newly recruited zealots—Toads wielding stolen town guard weaponry, wearing crude robes, and chanting discordant hymns of vengeance against 'The Betrayer Archie.' 

The combat was fierce and bloody. Markop led the vanguard. He drank a vial of *Kruglom Zizzl Grog*, his movements blurring with unnatural, jittery speed as he swept through the foyers and grand staircases, his blade a blur, clearing rooms with terrifying efficiency. When cultists clustered in choke points, Markop hurled *Puffbane Goblinbombs*, filling the corridors with noxious, hallucinogenic gas that left the zealots choking and weeping.

Archie provided heavy artillery support. Having learned nothing about collateral damage from previous encounters, he hurled firebolts and full fireballs down the velvet-lined hallways, scorching the Mayor's expensive historical tapestries, shattering antique crystal chandeliers, and setting fire to centuries-old mahogany furniture. The pirates, highly motivated by the prospect of looting a mayor's mansion, fought with cutlasses and flintlock pistols, screaming sea shanties as they traded fire with cultist crossbowmen.

They fought their way upward, leaving a trail of unconscious cultists and burning debris, until they reached the grand ballroom on the highest floor.

Markop kicked the double doors open.

There, floating three feet above the polished, blood-stained marble floor, bathed in the blinding, prismatic, almost painful light of the Crystal Star shard now embedded firmly in the head of his wooden staff, was the God Toad.

His eyes glowed with a terrifying, blank cosmic fury. The air around him crackled with static electricity and the sharp smell of ozone. The room's temperature had dropped twenty degrees, the chill of the void replacing the heat of the burning manor below.

'ARCHIE MISER!' the God Toad's voice boomed. It was no longer the reedy squeak of a commoner; it was amplified by divine acoustics, echoing off the vaulted ceilings with the force of thunder. 'YOU TOLD ME TO WAIT! YOU LEFT ME IN THE FIRE! AND NOW, YOU SHALL FACE THE ABSOLUTE JUDGMENT OF THE HEAVENS!'

Archie, squinting through the brilliant light of the Crystal Star, entirely failing to grasp the profound theological and personal weight of the moment, reportedly tilted his head and responded with:

'Do I know you?'

Waluigi considers this one of the most staggering tactical errors in recorded history. Archie did not recognize the man whose life he had ruined. He dismissed a god. 

This response elevated the God Toad's rage from 'vengeful' to 'apocalyptically unhinged.'

The God Toad shrieked, raising his star-tipped staff high above his head. He chanted a word of power that vibrated so intensely it rattled the fillings in the pirates' teeth and caused the glass in the windows to shatter outward. He pointed the staff directly at the party, declaring that they would be imprisoned in the void for eternity, held as suffering trophies of his divine wrath.

A massive, glowing, ethereal cage materialized from the ceiling, dropping with the speed of a guillotine, and slammed down heavily around Archie, Markop, and the pirates. The magical bars hummed with lethal, crackling energy. The trap was sprung. The heroes were caught. The villain began to laugh—a deep, booming, resonant laugh of absolute, final triumph.

And then, the party simply walked out.

Waluigi cannot overstate the comedic perfection of this catastrophic structural failure. 

The God Toad possessed the raw, unfiltered cosmic power to summon an indestructible magical prison directly from the ether. He had the power of the stars at his fingertips. However, the God Toad was, until very recently, just a guy with a stick. He had never studied architecture. He had no background in geometry. He possessed absolutely zero basic spatial reasoning skills. 

He had summoned a cage designed, proportionally, to hold a massive dragon.

The glowing, lethal magical bars of the cage were spaced approximately four and a half feet apart.

Archie looked at the bars. Markop looked at the bars. The pirates looked at the bars. The humming energy was deadly, but the gaps were massive. Without saying a single word, Markop simply turned his shoulders sideways and stepped comfortably through the huge gap between the glowing columns of energy. Archie, bewildered, followed him. The pirates, holding their looted silverware, strolled out after them. 

They did not have to cast a complex *dispel magic* incantation. They did not have to engage in a tense lock-picking mini-game. They just had to not be ten feet wide.

The God Toad's triumphant, booming laughter died in his throat, replaced by a choked gasp. He stared at his empty, comically oversized cage. He stared at the party, who were now standing entirely outside the cage, looking back at him with a mixture of profound confusion and intense secondhand embarrassment. 

The divine aura surrounding the Toad flickered violently. The sheer, crushing humiliation of the moment fractured his immense concentration. The power of the Crystal Star wavered as his self-doubt spiked.

'THIS IS NOT OVER!' the God Toad shrieked, his voice cracking and reverting back to its normal, reedy, pathetic Toad pitch. 'ARCHIE, YOU BETRAYED ME! I WILL HUNT YOU TO THE ENDS OF THE EARTH! YOU HEAR ME?! TO THE ENDS OF THE EARTH!'

With a blinding, concussive flash of light that temporarily blinded everyone in the room, the God Toad activated the Crystal Star shard and teleported away. The resulting energy discharge blasted a massive hole straight through the manor's roof, sending shingles and burning wood raining down. He vanished into the mist.

The moment he left, the magic sustaining the corruption faded. The blood in the fountains outside immediately congealed and turned back into foul, stagnant water. The surviving cultists downstairs dropped their weapons and surrendered to the local guard who were finally arriving.

The party stood in the ruined, burning ballroom. They had survived the sauna. They had defeated the cult. They had witnessed the birth of a deity. 

But they had also officially gained an immortal nemesis wielding a weapon of mass destruction, and they still had to get out of town before the vampire lords held them accountable for the property damage at the spa.

## Part V: Missing Time and the Grueling Road to Swiftsoul


The historical record becomes frustratingly, stubbornly thin at this juncture. Waluigi has attempted to trace the party's exact movements between leaving the ruined, smoking Mayor's Manor in Ravencreek and arriving at the towering gates of Swiftsoul Keep, but the data is fragmented, contradictory, or simply non-existent. 

What is known with certainty is that Archie and Markop successfully rendezvoused with Rakka. They delivered the bizarre alchemical ingredients they had fought so hard to procure. Rakka, satisfied with the transaction and entirely unbothered by the fact that Archie had nearly burned down a neighboring town to get them, provided the final confirmation regarding Markop's father.

The captors had indeed moved up the mountain. They were heading to Swiftsoul Keep, specifically seeking transport out of the region via the heavily guarded military airship docks.

The party—Archie, Markop, and the fiercely loyal, highly aromatic pirates—began the grueling ascent up the treacherous mountain paths toward Swiftsoul. The journey took several weeks. They moved through craggy, unforgiving terrain, battling freezing winds, dwindling supplies, and the constant threat of displaced dragon attacks from the skies above. They were exhausted, hungry, and moving deliberately toward a heavily militarized zone where they had absolutely zero legal standing and several active warrants for their arrest.

But they were not the only individuals heading toward a collision at Swiftsoul Keep.

## Part VI:


The Peebleton Caves, the Voicemail of Ruin, and the Wrong Blimp

While Archie and Markop were dealing with blood fountains, goblin alchemy, and angry ascended Toads, a completely separate and equally disastrous narrative was unfolding hundreds of miles to the east, deep within the subterranean labyrinth known as the Peebleton Caves.

Hjumpik, the stoic, battle-hardened warrior, and Bowser, the massive, geographically challenged King of the Koopas, had forged an alliance out of sheer survival necessity. They were attempting to navigate the lightless depths of the caves, operating under Bowser's loudly stated, completely inaccurate assertion that this route was a direct, secret shortcut back to the Mushroom Kingdom.

They had been guided for a time by a young, indigenous red dragon—a subterranean offshoot of the draconian family tree, not one of the ancient titans from the mountain, but a loyal companion nonetheless.

The journey through the dark was harrowing, and the red dragon companion did not survive it.

The details of what happened to this red dragon are sealed in a vault of silence that neither Hjumpik nor Bowser will willingly open. Waluigi, as a seasoned interrogator, respects the mechanics of profound trauma enough to not push for details he doesn't strictly need. When two individuals who are normally predisposed to violence, bragging, and extreme volume refuse to discuss an event, the event was likely gruesome, heartbreaking, and deeply personal. They lost their guide to the darkness, and they were forced to continue alone.

Eventually, exhausted and grieving, they stumbled upon an abandoned, dusty campsite in the deep caverns. Among the scattered, rotted detritus lay a heavy, battery-powered two-way radio, a remnant of the kingdom's fractured, pre-collapse communication infrastructure.

Bowser, hoping to find a distress frequency, a navigational beacon, or just the sound of another voice, activated it.

The radio crackled heavily with static, and then a voicemail began to play on a repeating loop.

Waluigi has procured the transcript of this recording, and he considers it a masterpiece of targeted, sociopathic psychological warfare. It was recorded by Wario. Wario was performing a flawless, entirely malicious, and shockingly accurate vocal impersonation of Mario. The recording began with bizarre, aggressive gorilline vocalizations, followed by a sharp dial tone, and then the message:

> *"Hello, everybody. It is a-me, Wari— uh, Mario!"*
>
> *"And I have a special message for all of my closest friends and-a family members... You mean completely nothing to me, beyond the 'gold-a' coins that you will inevitably drop when I hate-crime stomp you on your head, because you are so gay!"*
>
> *"That's right; I am a homophobe AND racist! Feel free to deplatform me from all social-media and ban me from public political discourse, as well as deface any effigies of me, especially ones that are large and difficult to maintain. I also do not mind if you were to mail me your excrement, as I wholly deserve an act such as this."*
>
> *"There have also been many instances of me viciously raping my brother Luigi and intimidating him into silence. Those of you having any issues with this announcement can come to my house and attack me, if you so dare! Preferably in the late hours of the night when most people would most likely be sleeping. I will be pretending to be asleep and ready to fight back. Do not hesitate to beat or maim me, as I am not afraid and can take many strong opponents at once, as I am sure you know from my staged gameplay."*
>
> *"Do not listen to any attempt to rescind this confession, as I am 'a-truly' a complete coward, and am only recording this under the influence of drugs and alcohol, which I routinely consume, especially before any public appearances and operating complex machinery."*
>
> *"I will now seize the opportunity, while helplessly in the throes of my illicit substances, to confess my admiration for the late Wario, who surpassed me in every skill I am famous for, in every possible sense. I have always envied him and his great wealth, and only brought down Warioland™ out of my terrible jealousy and fear of coming to assassinate me in a cunning scheme to emasculate my legacy."*
>
> *"I thank Mushroom God every day that 'he-a' took his own life, and no longer threaten my iron grip on the dirty peasants that worship me. And by the way, I demand you cease all speculation and conspiracy theories postulating that Wario is in fact alive. He is dead, okay? I personally investigated his fake suicide, and saw his dead body and he released his death-fart into my face as my mouth hung open from the terrible sight."*
>
> *"Do not pursue any more notions or clues about his whereabouts. I already told you that we disposed of his body in the Oho Ocean! So, no more posting of hoax sighting pictures to the 4Wario image boards! Let me- uh, ...HIM rest in peace, and maybe his cheeky spirit will better sit with us all..."*
>
> *"So to recap; I am a drug-addict rapist, I hate you, and I beg capable individuals to come maim and/or dominate me by 'a-surprise'. If you are still not enraged by this message, I ask you to play it again until you are, please. 'Fuck-a' you, and come and get me!"*
>
> *(Dial tone).*

Waluigi must document the sheer, unrelenting, strategic malice of this recording. The slip at the beginning—'Wari— uh, Mario!'—was intentional. Wario designed this message not just to utterly destroy Mario's public reputation by having him 'confess' to drug addiction, cowardice, and horrific abuse of Luigi, but also to aggressively, preemptively reinforce the public narrative that Wario himself was dead. It was a dual-purpose propaganda strike broadcast across the Midland's emergency frequencies to cover his tracks while he smuggled stolen goods.

Bowser and Hjumpik, sitting in a dark cave, covered in grime, having just lost a friend, listened to this recording in its entirety.

They had no context for Wario's sophisticated misinformation campaigns. They heard the voice of the Mushroom Kingdom's greatest hero confessing to being an irredeemable monster. They looked at the rusted radio, looked at each other, and formed a devastatingly logical, entirely incorrect conclusion: Mario was evil, the Mushroom Kingdom's leadership was a corrupt lie, and everything they thought they knew about heroism was false.

This false paradigm shift would color their interactions with the world, and with each other, for months to come. It forged a grim bond between them.

## Section IX:


The Wrong Blimp to Swiftsoul

Fuelled by disgust at the voicemail and the lingering trauma of the caves, Bowser and Hjumpik finally battered their way through the final rockfalls and reached the surface. They emerged blinking into the smoky, soot-stained daylight, fully expecting to see the green borders of the Mushroom Kingdom.

They had exited on the completely wrong side of the continent.

Bowser's navigational intuition had failed them with a precision that bordered on the mathematical. They were stranded in a barren, rocky, windswept valley miles from anywhere.

In the distance, a massive commercial transport blimp was hovering low, taking on emergency refugees fleeing the expanding dragon crisis in the north.

Having absolutely no other options, and refusing to go back into the caves, Bowser and Hjumpik flagged it down and boarded. They paid their fare in scavenged gems.

Bowser immediately demanded to know when they would arrive at the Mushroom Kingdom. The terrified pilot, staring up at a massive, blood-stained, heavily armed Koopa, informed him in a trembling voice that this blimp was heading strictly north. It was ascending into the high mountain peaks, bound for the military aerodrome and trade hub of Swiftsoul Keep.

Bowser was furious. The blimp was heading in the exact opposite direction of his intended destination. He spent the entire multi-day journey pacing the gondola of the blimp, terrifying the civilian passengers. He complained loudly and incessantly about the altitude, the lack of legroom, the incompetence of Midland cartography, the smell of the other passengers, and the fundamental injustice of a universe that kept moving his kingdom further away from him. 

Hjumpik sat in silence, anchoring the duo's sanity as the blimp slowly ascended into the freezing, mist-choked clouds.

## Part X: Swiftsoul Keep —


The Lower Levels, the Fighting Arena, and Gary the Fake Dragon

When the blimp finally docked, Hjumpik and Bowser disembarked into Swiftsoul Keep. 

Swiftsoul is a sprawling, multi-tiered fortress city of stone and steel carved into the side of a mountain. It is divided into strict hierarchies. The upper levels are pristine, housing the Royal military command, the primary airship docks, and the magistrates' courts where 'justice' is dispensed to those who can afford it. The lower levels are a grimy, smog-choked, claustrophobic underbelly of mechanics, smugglers, off-duty guards, and illicit entertainment.

Hjumpik and Bowser, needing coin and a way to burn off their mounting, violent aggression, wandered into the lower levels and discovered a subterranean fighting pit. The air was thick with the smell of cheap ale, sweat, ozone, and cigar smoke. Hundreds of off-duty mercenaries, dock workers, and criminals were screaming at the bloodstained sand below.

The promoters of the arena were actively hyping their main event. The chalkboard signs surrounding the pit read in crude lettering: *TONIGHT ONLY! SURVIVE THE TERROR OF THE PEAKS! BATTLE A REAL DRAGON! 500 GOLD PURSE!*

Hjumpik, severely lacking in funds and entirely unafraid of reptiles after his experiences, signed the bloody ledger and stepped down into the pit.

The crowd roared, throwing half-empty mugs into the sand. The massive iron portcullis at the far end of the arena slowly ground upward. Chains rattled ominously. The announcer screamed into a megaphone, introducing the terrifying beast that had supposedly ravaged the Midlands.

Out walked a man named Gary.

Gary was wearing a dragon costume. It was not a good costume. It was not even a passable costume. It was constructed of hastily painted cardboard, cheap green felt, and highly visible duct tape holding the tail on. Gary was holding two large sparklers in his hands to simulate 'fire breath.' He shuffled into the center of the ring, looking profoundly apologetic and slightly hungover, and let out a half-hearted, muffled roar through the papier-mâché snout that sounded more like a cough.

Hjumpik lowered his heavy axe, staring at Gary with flat, unamused, absolute exhaustion.

Up in the cheap seats, leaning over the iron railing, Bowser was watching.

Waluigi must pause to analyze the psychological state of the Koopa King in this exact second. Bowser is a proud, massive, fire-breathing creature with deep draconic heritage. He views himself as the apex predator of the natural order. Furthermore, he had literally *just* lost a real, noble red dragon companion in the dark of the Peebleton Caves—a traumatic loss he was actively suppressing beneath layers of bravado.

When Bowser looked down into the pit and saw Gary shuffling around in green felt holding sparklers, he did not just see a fraudulent business practice. He saw a profound, unforgivable insult to the majesty of dragons. He saw stolen valor. He saw a mockery of the noble creature he had just mourned in the dark.

Bowser's vision went entirely red.

He did not walk down the stairs to the pit. He vaulted over the railing. A thousand pounds of spiked shell, scaled muscle, and pure rage plummeted forty feet through the air. He crashed into the center of the fighting pit with a tectonic impact that shattered the stone floor, kicked up a massive cloud of dust, and knocked Gary the Fake Dragon entirely out of his felt suit by the sheer force of the shockwave.

The screaming crowd went dead silent.

Bowser stood up slowly from the crater. He inhaled deeply, his chest expanding, the intense heat radiating from his jaws noticeably distorting the air around him.

'YOU WANT TO SEE A REAL DRAGON?!' Bowser roared, his voice shaking the very foundations of the arena and rattling the mugs on the tables.

He unleashed a torrent of actual, blinding, localized hellfire directly into the ceiling, instantly incinerating the promotional banners, melting the announcer's megaphone into slag, and scorching the stone black.

The silence broke. Absolute, terrifying panic erupted. The crowd screamed and stampeded for the narrow exits, trampling each other in their desperation to flee. 

Arena security—a dozen large, heavily armored trolls wielding iron-shod clubs—rushed the pit, intending to subdue the beast ruining their profit margin.

Hjumpik looked at Bowser. Bowser looked at Hjumpik. Without exchanging a single word, they formed a defensive perimeter, standing back-to-back in the sand, and prepared to violently dismantle the entire security force of the Swiftsoul lower levels.

## Part VIII:


The Convergence in the Pit

At this exact, precise moment, the heavy double doors of the arena concourse burst open.

Archie and Markop sprinted through, running for their lives.

They had arrived in Swiftsoul days prior and had immediately found themselves entangled in the upper-level politics. Their investigation into Markop's father's disappearance had led them straight into a conspiracy involving the Iron Fists guild, explosive smuggling, and the impending catastrophe at the blimp station. They were currently fleeing the authorities and had ducked into the lower levels hoping to lose their pursuers in the slums.

Instead, they ran face-first into a full-scale riot caused by a giant turtle breathing fire on security trolls.

Markop skidded to a halt on the balcony, looking down at the pit. He saw Hjumpik, a warrior he had never met, swinging an axe with terrifying, mechanical precision, holding off three trolls at once. He saw Bowser, tossing armored guards into the bleachers like ragdolls while roaring.

'Who is the turtle?' Archie yelled over the din of screaming patrons and breaking furniture.

'I don't know, but he's winning,' Markop replied, his tactical mind instantly assessing the variables. 'Let's help him.'

Markop and Archie vaulted into the pit, landing beside Hjumpik and Bowser. Markop's sword joined Hjumpik's axe. Archie's wildly inaccurate fire magic joined Bowser's breath.

This was the moment. The crucible. Four distinct, highly dangerous individuals, brought together by a chaotic combination of kidnapped fathers, fake dragons, exploding blimps, and terrible geography, standing in a circle of violence against the authorities of Swiftsoul Keep. They did not formalize an alliance. They did not shake hands. They did not even exchange names. They simply recognized that they were all currently committing multiple felonies in the same room, they were surrounded by enemies, and survival dictated immediate cooperation.

Disaster Inc. was born in the blood, fire, and sawdust of a scam arena.

## Part IX:


The Trial, The Vigilance, and Leaving the Ground

They fought their way out of the arena, leaving a trail of unconscious trolls and burning debris behind them, but the law eventually caught up in the upper levels. 

The events that immediately followed—the arrest of Archie Miser for the Swiftsoul Station explosion, the chaotic courtroom trial prosecuted by the relentless, terrifyingly competent Miles Edgeworth, the introduction of Waluigi's 'Wheel of Regret,' and the devastating revelations regarding Commander G, X.O., and Wario's explosive sabotage—are matters of extensive public record. Waluigi has documented them thoroughly in separate legal archives and will not duplicate them here.

What matters is the outcome. The trial dissolved into complete chaos. The evidence was compromised by Iron Fists interference. The newly formed party realized that legal exoneration was impossible in a justice system rigged by mercenaries, corrupt magistrates, and Wario's double-dealing.

The only option was flight. Not just leaving the town, but leaving the ground entirely.

The party—Archie, Markop, Hjumpik, and Bowser—broke out of the courtroom, fighting past the bailiffs, and sprinted for the upper military docks. 

There, secured to the primary mooring mast, was the *Vigilance*. A state-of-the-art, military-grade Regal Empire airship. It was sleek, heavily armed, armored in dark iron, and currently fueling for departure.

They stormed the docking gantry. They overpowered the minimal skeletal crew on board with shocking violence. Archie rushed to the helm and fired up the arcane engines, entirely ignoring the safety protocols and pre-flight checklists. The massive propellers whined to life, biting into the thin, freezing mountain air.

As the *Vigilance* snapped its heavy mooring lines, taking a chunk of the dock with it, and lurched violently away from the mountain, Archie ran to the aft railing.

Down below, standing on the mist-slicked wooden planks of the ruined pier, were Captain Sugar's pirates. The crew that had followed them from the burning ruins of Edgeshade, sweated with them in the Veilwood sauna, and stormed the blood-drenched Mayor's Manor.

They were looking up at the ascending ship.

There was no room for them. Airships are for international fugitives; pirates belong to the sea and the mud. 

Archie waved back at them. Markop stood silently beside him, watching the ground fall away. Hjumpik immediately went below decks to check the ship's armory. Bowser began wandering the corridors, looking for the captain's quarters to claim the largest bed as his royal right.

The *Vigilance* broke through the heavy cloud cover, ascending into the clear, freezing blue sky above the Midlands. They were no longer grounded adventurers. They were a unified crew of outlaws, in possession of stolen, highly classified military hardware, heading toward a horizon filled with floating cities, dimensional rifts, and consequences they could not even begin to fathom.

The first session of their lives had ended. The true nightmare had just begun.

WAH.

keyBattles.outcome: Trap bypassed. The party was reunited and aware that the Cult of the God Toad was actively hunting them.

keyBattles.name: The Siege of the Mayor's Manor
keyBattles.description: The party and the pirates assaulted the manor to stop the God Toad's ascension ritual. They fought room-by-room through fanatic cultists using Markop's newly minted Blazefizz Gloomvials and Archie's fire magic.
keyBattles.outcome: Ritual disrupted. The God Toad attempted to cage them, failed miserably due to poor bar spacing, and teleported away while declaring his eternal grudge.

keyBattles.name: The Swiftsoul Arena Riot
keyBattles.description: Hjumpik was engaged in a sanctioned pit fight against Gary, the fake dragon. Bowser, insulted by the stolen draconic valor, vaulted into the ring to demand a real fight and breathed fire on the ceiling. This triggered a massive brawl with arena security trolls, which Archie and Markop joined while fleeing the authorities.
keyBattles.outcome: The arena dissolved into absolute chaos, allowing Hjumpik, Bowser, Archie, and Markop to fight back-to-back, formally cementing their alliance and facilitating their escape to the upper docks.
