summary: On the first day of Efferd, 1040 BF, the fragile geopolitical stability of the Midlands was permanently shattered by an act of unprecedented greed and staggering collateral consequence. A young fire mage named Archie Miser and a pragmatic fighter named Markop climbed Dragon Mountain during the regional Festival of Stars. They were preceded by a heavily armed detachment of the Iron Fists mercenary guild. At the summit, waiting amidst the obsidian crags, sat an ancient red dragon guarding a clutch of highly coveted Gold Dragon eggs. Unbeknownst to the Iron Fists, Archie, or Markop, Wario and Waluigi had already infiltrated the summit. Wario—operating under the absurdly fraudulent legal guise of a 'noble warrior on a quest'—and Waluigi, an arcane practitioner who considers chaos an art form, stole the Gold Dragon eggs. These specific eggs were targeted for the Nocturnaether Conclave, a subterranean sect of vampiric acolytes who required the draconic embryos for their 'Eclipsarcanum Phasemelds' rituals. The theft enraged the ancient guardian, resulting in the immediate incineration of the Iron Fists and a tectonic eruption. Millions of slumbering dragons poured from the mountain's ruptured interior, blanketing the Regal Empire in fire and shadow. In the immediate aftermath, the town of Edgeshade was burned to ash. During the evacuation, Markop's father was captured by unknown assailants, a crew of opportunistic pirates was recruited, and Archie casually abandoned a nameless Toad who would subsequently discover a Crystal Star shard and ascend to become the vengeful 'God Toad.' Concurrently, hundreds of miles away in the Peebleton Caves, Bowser and a warrior named Hjumpik lost a red dragon companion, discovered an abandoned two-way radio containing a devastatingly slanderous voicemail recorded by Wario impersonating Mario, and accidentally boarded a blimp heading the wrong direction toward Swiftsoul Keep. Waluigi has meticulously reconstructed this origin event, dedicating thousands of words to analyzing the intersecting motivations, the tragic miscommunications, and the precise mathematical volume of Wario's avarice. Every airship hijacking, every planar fracture, every vampire encounter, and every frozen Luigi block that followed traces back to this single mountain. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting the first day of the 1040 BF crisis because the first day is where the pathological pattern of 'Disaster Inc.' established itself. Everything this group would become—the collateral damage, the accidental heroism, the tendency to create problems of continental scale while attempting to solve problems of personal scale, and the sheer, unadulterated velocity of their bad decisions—was already visible on Dragon Mountain. Except it was not in miniature. It was immediately scaled to millions of dragons.

Waluigi is also documenting this day because nobody else has documented it with the requisite combination of historical accuracy and ruthless psychological dissection. Archie Miser has never given a complete account of what happened on the mountain because Archie's relationship with complete accounts is approximately as stable as his relationship with fire safety. Markop has discussed it only in fragmented, tactical debriefs, carefully avoiding the emotional weight of witnessing his father's capture. Hjumpik was in a different location entirely, navigating a subterranean nightmare. Bowser's account of the Peebleton Caves is colored by Bowser's specific relationship with objective truth, which is that he values it intensely when it flatters him and treats it as entirely decorative when it does not.

Waluigi was on the mountain. Waluigi stole the eggs. Waluigi will provide the definitive account, sparing no one, especially not himself.

## Section I:


The Nocturnaether Conclave and the Gold Dragon Economy

To understand why Dragon Mountain erupted, one must first understand *why* Wario and Waluigi were on the summit, and *what* they were stealing. It was not a simple smash-and-grab for shiny objects. It was a highly calculated interception of a black-market arcane supply chain.

Within the subterranean abyss of the Midlands, a sect known as the Nocturnaether Conclave operates. These vampiric acolytes delve into the esoteric nexus between draconic life force and unholy power. According to intercepted texts from the Umbral Codex, these vampires initiate arcane communions during specific celestial alignments known as 'Eclipsarcanum Phasemelds.' At these rare junctures, the inherent, radiant energies within a Gold Dragon egg align with the ambient umbral currents of the underworld, creating a mystical resonance.

During these rituals, the vampiric acolytes wield specially crafted 'Aetherdrain Phylacteries'—enchanted vessels designed to siphon the Gold Dragon egg's ethereal radiance. The phylacteries act as conduits, drawing upon the cosmic potential of the unborn dragon while subtly infusing the vampiric essence within the unholy order. The acolytes perform a ritualistic dance known as the 'Nocturnaether Umbradance,' accompanied by haunting incantations that establish a metaphysical link between the vampires and the golden embryo.

In the final stages of the ritual, the acolytes unleash the 'Nexusrift Dracotome,' a vampiric relic inscribed with forbidden glyphs that resonate with the dragon's embryonic dreams. As the Dracotome hovers over the egg, it concentrates the amalgamated energies into a harmonious blend of celestial and vampiric power. The Nocturnaether Conclave believes that by intertwining the Gold Dragon's cosmic potential with their own ambitions, they can attain unparalleled mastery over shadows, time, and arcane forces.

Gold Dragon eggs are, therefore, not just rare; they are the single most valuable ritual component in the Midlands' supernatural underworld. The vampires of Fairth's Retreat and the Nocturnaether Conclave were willing to pay astronomical sums for them.

Wario knew this.

## Section II:


The Facade of the Noble Warrior and the Chaos Mage

Waluigi must pause to document the sheer bureaucratic absurdity of how Wario and Waluigi moved through the Midlands without being immediately arrested. 

According to official Regal Empire and local Guild registries, *Wario is a formidable warrior who swears allegiance to rulers, religious orders, and noble causes. Wario's alignment dictates the degree to which he upholds his pledges. Whether embarking on a quest or safeguarding a realm, Wario typically journeys with a retinue that includes squires and hirelings who are commoners.*

Waluigi types these words with a profound sense of linguistic nausea. The fact that Wario managed to file paperwork registering himself as a 'noble warrior safeguarding realms' is a testament to the catastrophic gullibility of the Midlands' administrative clerks. Wario used this classification to bypass checkpoints, commandeer supplies, and claim 'diplomatic immunity' while actively plotting to steal from an ancient draconic nesting ground. The 'squires and hirelings' mentioned in his registry were usually just unfortunate locals he had bullied into carrying his luggage before abandoning them at the first sign of danger.

Waluigi's own official classification was slightly more accurate, though equally weaponized. *Mages spend their lives delving into the arcane mysteries, and Waluigi is no exception. Unlike other mages who may advise nobles or conduct isolated experiments, Waluigi's magical prowess is often overshadowed by his mischievous nature. He thrives on creating chaos and mischief through his magical abilities.*

This is true. Waluigi respects the architecture of magic, but he respects the collapse of architecture even more. When Wario proposed stealing the Gold Dragon eggs to sell to the Nocturnaether vampires, Waluigi did not agree because he needed the gold. He agreed because the sheer, fractal complexity of the chaos it would cause—involving vampires, dragons, guilds, and empires—was an artistic endeavor too magnificent to pass up.

## Section III:


The Ascent of Archie and Markop 

On the morning of 1 Efferd, while Wario and Waluigi were already nearing the summit, Archie Miser and Markop began their ascent from the lower slopes. 

Archie and Markop were young. This detail matters. The Archie and Markop who would later navigate the Vigilance airship crisis, survive Raventree Manor's planar collapse, and become central figures in a multi-dimensional catastrophe were not yet those hardened operatives. They were kids climbing a mountain because the mountain was there, because the Festival of Stars was scheduled for that evening in nearby Edgeshade, and because mountains are the kind of thing young people without sufficient survival instincts decide to conquer.

The ascent was ecologically and magically compromised from the beginning. Waluigi, observing from a higher vantage point, noted the profound oddities of the lower slopes.

Dancing goblins. Inside a treasure chest. 

Archie and Markop encountered a massive, open wooden chest. It was not filled with gold, nor was it a mimic attempting to consume them. It was filled with goblins, performing an intricate, choreographed dance routine. They were not guarding the chest; they were utilizing it as a stage. The goblins were performing with a sense of pride and practice that suggested an audience, though none was present.

Waluigi, a student of the arcane and the bizarre, recognizes this as a manifestation of extreme ambient fey magic leaking from the mountain's subterranean depths. The presence of these goblins was a literal, screaming ecological warning that the mountain's normal rules had been suspended. It was also an environment rich in highly specific, volatile alchemical ingredients. (It was precisely these types of goblin-adjacent components that Markop would later spend time learning to harvest and brew with the Rakasha—creating concoctions like the 'Goblim Brew Elix,' the 'Grog of Invisibl'ty,' the 'Goblinkfire Ess'nce,' and the 'Sneaky Sneak Serum.' The roots of Markop's later alchemical proficiency began here, walking past a chest of dancing fey creatures).

Archie and Markop looked at the dancing goblins, registered the sight as unusual, and simply continued climbing.

This was the first documented instance of the pattern that would define Disaster Inc.: encountering something deeply strange, noting it, and proceeding forward without adequate investigation. They walked past the warning.

## Section IV:


The Iron Fists and the Ancient Red

Archie and Markop were not the only organized force on the slopes. They were soon overtaken by a heavily armed detachment of Iron Fist soldiers. 

Waluigi wants to be extremely precise: these were the *Iron Fists*, the mercenary guild chapter operating under Commander G, not the Iron Legion. The Iron Fists were ascending with military precision, in strict formation, clad in heat-resistant armor and carrying specialized draconic containment gear. They moved with the deliberate, chilling confidence of soldiers who had been ordered to climb a dragon's mountain and did not possess the imagination to question those orders. 

The Iron Fists' presence on Dragon Mountain on the day of the eruption was not coincidental. Military organizations do not deploy specialized anti-dragon infantry on the day of a local festival unless they have high-level intelligence. Someone in the guild leadership—perhaps Commander G, perhaps her chaotic kamidere daughter X.O., or perhaps a sub-contractor acting on behalf of the Nocturnaether Conclave—knew the Gold Dragon eggs were vulnerable. The Iron Fists were there to secure the payload.

They reached the summit. They found the payload.

They did not survive finding it.

The summit of Dragon Mountain was a broad, flattened expanse of scorched, obsidian stone, vitrified by centuries of sustained, unimaginable heat. The air shimmered with thermal distortion, carrying a scent Waluigi describes as 'copper, ozone, and the inside of a furnace that has been burning since the dawn of recorded history.'

At the center of this plateau sat the ancient red dragon.

Waluigi has seen many things. He has navigated planar tears, survived fairy courts, and maintained his composure in the presence of aristocratic vampires. But this dragon was the largest living organism Waluigi has ever laid eyes upon. Its red scales looked less like biological growth and more like geological strata, deep and saturated. Its folded wings resembled cliff faces. Its amber eyes possessed an ancient, malevolent intelligence that transcended animal instinct.

Behind the ancient red lay the nest: a depression in the stone worn smooth by centuries of bulk, holding the shimmering, massive Gold Dragon eggs.

The Iron Fist soldiers crested the ridge and fanned out, raising their containment weapons. 

The dragon burned them alive.

Waluigi must specify what 'burned them alive' means in this context, because the phrase is often overused. This was not a jet of flame. This was not a targeted attack. The dragon simply exhaled. The exhalation carried a wall of thermal annihilation the way wind carries dust. The soldiers did not have time to scream, raise their shields, or deploy their magic. The ambient heat arrived before the visible flames, vaporizing the moisture in their lungs instantly. Their heat-resistant armor melted into slag, fusing to their skin before they were reduced to carbon silhouettes. In less than three seconds, an elite mercenary squad became a smudge of ash on the obsidian stone.

The dragon settled back into its resting position with the unhurried satisfaction of a creature that had casually swatted a mosquito.

Archie and Markop, arriving at the ridge just in time to witness this absolute localized apocalypse, made the only rational, survivable, intellectually defensible decision available to two young people.

They turned around and ran back down the mountain.

## Section V:


The Theft and the Eruption

They were too late.

While the dragon was occupied incinerating the Iron Fists, Wario and Waluigi had already bypassed the beast's peripheral vision. Wario, driven by a greed so pure it practically generated its own gravitational field, had infiltrated the nest. 

When Archie and Markop turned to flee, they saw Wario and Waluigi sprinting down a secondary ridge. Wario's arms were full of the massive Gold Dragon eggs, his face split into a manic, horrifying grin. Waluigi was beside him, utilizing his long, lanky stride to maximum efficiency, carrying his own share of the stolen clutch. 

They were stealing the exact items the Nocturnaether Conclave needed for their 'Eclipsarcanum Phasemelds.' They were stealing the future of the draconic race. 

And the ancient red dragon noticed.

What followed was not a roar. It was not a localized attack. It was an awakening. The ancient red dragon reared back and released a sound that did not just travel through the air; it traveled through the bedrock. It was a seismic command. It was the activation of a biological failsafe that had been dormant for millennia.

Dragon Mountain erupted. 

Not with magma. The mountain physically split apart. The obsidian slopes cracked along massive fault lines. From deep inside the subterranean chambers, caverns, and hollows that stretched down into the planet's mantle, dragons emerged.

Millions of them.

Waluigi does not exaggerate numbers when documenting crises. It was millions. They poured from the ruptured mountain like bats fleeing a flooded cave, except each bat was the size of a galleon and breathed elemental destruction. The sky above the Midlands instantly went dark—not from smoke, but from the sheer, overlapping mass of draconic bodies blocking out the sun. The sound of millions of wings beating simultaneously created a bass vibration that made teeth ache and vision blur. 

The swarm ascended, circled the shattered peak, and then surged southward, spreading out like a wave of biblical judgment across the Regal Empire.

The dragon crisis had begun. A crisis that would alter the political and physical landscape of the continent, sever supply lines, dictate military deployments, and follow the party like a shadow for the foreseeable future. 

Wario and Waluigi kept running. Archie and Markop ran faster.

## Section VI:


The Githyanki Samurai House

The descent was a nightmare of falling rocks, screaming wildlife, and the relentless, deafening roar of the sky. Between the base of Dragon Mountain and the town of Edgeshade, Archie and Markop stumbled upon a structure that defied all regional logic.

It was a house built in the exact architectural style of a samurai estate—sliding paper screens, polished wooden floors, perfectly angled eaves, and a meticulously raked zen garden. This structure sat amid the burning, cracking Midlands wilderness as if it had been dropped there from orbit.

Inside were Githyanki.

Waluigi documents this because the presence of Githyanki—tall, angular, yellow-skinned extraplanar warriors—at the epicenter of a draconic eruption is not a coincidence. The Githyanki are known planar travelers and hunters, possessing an ancient, codified enmity with certain draconic factions and deep ties to the Astral Plane. Their presence in a samurai-styled outpost at the exact moment Dragon Mountain ruptured suggests they were either monitoring the mountain, hunting a specific target, or utilizing the massive release of magical energy to mask their own planar transit.

Archie and Markop burst into the house, desperately seeking shelter from the falling debris. The details of their interaction with the Githyanki are frantic and fragmented. It is unclear whether they fought the extraplanar warriors, negotiated a frantic truce, or simply caused so much confusion that they were able to sprint through the estate and out the back doors. 

What is known is that the house acted as an impossible spatial shortcut. They entered near the base of the mountain and exited almost directly onto the outskirts of Edgeshade, having bypassed several miles of treacherous terrain through a building that likely existed in two places at once.

## Section VII:


The Siege of Edgeshade and the Birth of the God Toad

Edgeshade was a modest, resilient town known primarily for its annual 'Festival of Stars.' The festival was a celebration of celestial alignments, featuring paper lanterns, night markets, and communal astronomy. 

The festival was scheduled for that evening. The mountain erupted in the afternoon. The dragons arrived at sunset.

Waluigi did not witness the destruction of Edgeshade firsthand; he and Wario were currently securing their stolen Gold Dragon eggs in an undisclosed location. However, Waluigi has reconstructed the horror from Archie and Markop's accounts and the subsequent grim reports from the Regal Empire's disaster relief agencies.

The dragon swarm hit Edgeshade not as a coordinated military strike, but as an ecological disaster. Fire rained from the sky. The paper lanterns and festive banners ignited instantly. The mushroom-houses and timber structures, never designed to withstand sustained incendiary bombardment, collapsed into roaring pyres. The streets became rivers of panic.

Archie and Markop ran through the burning town, surrounded by screaming civilians, collapsing roofs, and the overwhelming heat of a settlement being erased from the map. 

In the midst of this chaos, tragedy struck with surgical precision. Markop's father, who had been attending the festival, was captured. 

He was not incidentally killed or trapped under rubble. He was actively snatched in the confusion by unknown assailants. Whether these were opportunistic slavers, cultists taking advantage of the panic, or agents of a deeper conspiracy (perhaps even the Nocturnaether Conclave utilizing the distraction), the result was the same. Markop watched helplessly as his father was dragged away into the smoke. 

The immediate requirement for survival overrode the immediate ability to pursue. Markop was forced to keep moving to avoid being incinerated.

They reached a heavy stone tavern on the town's outskirts. Unlike the timber homes, the tavern's thick masonry was resisting the flames. 

Inside, it was being systematically looted. 

A crew of rough, soot-stained pirates—later identified as belonging to Captain Sugar's fleet—were ignoring the apocalyptic destruction outside and focusing entirely on rolling barrels of expensive rum and lifting lockboxes out the back door. They were accompanied by a brightly colored, remarkably calm parrot that seemed to be barking orders.

Archie and Markop, recognizing that surviving a dragon siege is statistically more probable in a group, burst into the tavern and confronted the looters. The ensuing interaction was less of a negotiation and more of a mutual recognition of desperate circumstances. The pirates, realizing the town was seconds away from total collapse, agreed to let the two teenagers join their escape party. The sheer chaos forged an immediate, pragmatic alliance between an aspiring mage, a traumatized fighter, and a crew of opportunistic maritime criminals.

They fled the tavern together, pushing through the burning outskirts.

Along the way, they picked up a survivor. It was a generic, completely unremarkable Toad carrying a simple wooden staff. He was huddled in an alleyway, terrified and alone. Archie, displaying a rare moment of apparent empathy, told the Toad to follow them.

Minutes later, the situation deteriorated further. Markop, unable to suppress the agonizing knowledge of his father's capture, spotted a break in the flames and made a definitive choice. He split off from the group, diving back into the danger zone to pursue his father's captors. The desperate quest that would define Markop's actions for the next several months had begun.

Archie was left leading the pirates and the nameless Toad. The dragons were making a final, devastating pass over the sector. The heat was unbearable. 

Archie turned to the nameless Toad. 

'Wait here,' Archie said. 'I'll be right back.'

Archie Miser then turned around, ran in the opposite direction with the pirates, and absolutely, unconditionally, never came back.

He abandoned the Toad in a burning town under a sky full of dragons.

Waluigi must emphasize the cosmic significance of this specific act of cowardice. 

The nameless Toad waited. He waited as the flames crept closer. He waited as he realized he had been lied to and left to die by a 'hero.' And in that moment of profound, agonizing betrayal, the sky above Edgeshade tore open.

A full, brilliant, reality-warping Crystal Star shard plummeted from the heavens. It crashed through the smoke and landed directly at the abandoned Toad's feet. 

The Toad, fueled by a sudden, consuming hatred for Archie Miser and empowered by an artifact of limitless cosmic potential, picked up the shard. He fused it with his wooden staff. He did not die in Edgeshade. He ascended. The trauma of abandonment crystallized into a divine complex. 

The God Toad was born in the ashes of the Festival of Stars, and his very first commandment to himself was the eventual, total annihilation of Archie Miser.

Archie and the pirates, entirely unaware that they had just catalyzed the birth of a vengeful deity, managed to escape the burning town and began the long, miserable trek toward the settlement of Ravencreek.

## Section VIII:


The Peebleton Caves and the Voicemail of Ruin

While the surface of the Midlands was burning, a parallel disaster of a more psychological nature was unfolding deep underground, far to the east in the Peebleton Caves.

Bowser, the King of the Koopas, and Hjumpik, a stoic warrior, were traversing the subterranean labyrinth. Bowser had confidently asserted that this cave system was a direct shortcut back to the Mushroom Kingdom. Bowser's geographical confidence is legendary, absolute, and almost always disastrously incorrect. 

They had allied quickly. Bowser respects durability, and Hjumpik is practically made of it. They were accompanied by a red dragon companion—a smaller, subterranean offshoot of the draconian family tree, not one of the ancient titans from the mountain, but a loyal guide nonetheless.

The journey through the dark was harrowing, and the red dragon companion did not survive it. 

The details of the dragon's death remain entirely undisclosed. Neither Bowser nor Hjumpik will speak of it. Waluigi respects the architecture of traumatic silence; when two individuals who are normally predisposed to violence and volume refuse to discuss an event, the event was likely gruesome, heartbreaking, and deeply personal. They lost their guide, and they continued in the dark.

Eventually, they stumbled upon an abandoned campsite in the deep caverns. Among the detritus lay a battery-powered two-way radio, a remnant of the kingdom's fractured communication infrastructure. 

Bowser, hoping to find a distress frequency or a navigational beacon, activated it. 

The radio crackled with static, and then a voicemail began to play. 

Waluigi has procured the transcript of this recording. It is a masterpiece of targeted psychological warfare. It was recorded by Wario, performing an unsettlingly accurate vocal impersonation of Mario. The recording began with bizarre, aggressive gorilline vocalizations, followed by a dial tone, and then the message:

*"Hello, everybody. It is a-me, Wari— uh, Mario!"*

*"And I have a special message for all of my closest friends and-a family members... You mean completely nothing to me, beyond the 'gold-a' coins that you will inevitably drop when I hate-crime stomp you on your head, because you are so gay!"*

*"That's right; I am a homophobe AND racist! Feel free to deplatform me from all social-media and ban me from public political discourse, as well as deface any effigies of me, especially ones that are large and difficult to maintain. I also do not mind if you were to mail me your excrement, as I wholly deserve an act such as this."*

*"There have also been many instances of me viciously raping my brother Luigi and intimidating him into silence. Those of you having any issues with this announcement can come to my house and attack me, if you so dare! Preferably in the late hours of the night when most people would most likely be sleeping. I will be pretending to be asleep and ready to fight back. Do not hesitate to beat or maim me, as I am not afraid and can take many strong opponents at once, as I am sure you know from my staged gameplay."*

*"Do not listen to any attempt to rescind this confession, as I am 'a-truly' a complete coward, and am only recording this under the influence of drugs and alcohol, which I routinely consume, especially before any public appearances and operating complex machinery."*

*"I will now seize the opportunity, while helplessly in the throes of my illicit substances, to confess my admiration for the late Wario, who surpassed me in every skill I am famous for, in every possible sense. I have always envied him and his great wealth, and only brought down Warioland™ out of my terrible jealousy and fear of coming to assassinate me in a cunning scheme to emasculate my legacy."*

*"I thank Mushroom God every day that 'he-a' took his own life, and no longer threaten my iron grip on the dirty peasants that worship me. And by the way, I demand you cease all speculation and conspiracy theories postulating that Wario is in fact alive. He is dead, okay? I personally investigated his fake suicide, and saw his dead body and he released his death-fart into my face as my mouth hung open from the terrible sight."*

*"Do not pursue any more notions or clues about his whereabouts. I already told you that we disposed of his body in the Oho Ocean! So, no more posting of hoax sighting pictures to the 4Wario image boards! Let me- uh, ...HIM rest in peace, and maybe his cheeky spirit will better sit with us all..."*

*"So to recap; I am a drug-addict rapist, I hate you, and I beg capable individuals to come maim and/or dominate me by 'a-surprise'. If you are still not enraged by this message, I ask you to play it again until you are, please. 'Fuck-a' you, and come and get me!"*

*(Dial tone).* 

Waluigi must document the sheer, unrelenting sociopathy of this recording. The slip at the beginning—'Wari— uh, Mario!'—was intentional. Wario designed this message not just to destroy Mario's reputation by confessing to drug addiction, cowardice, and horrific abuse of Luigi, but also to aggressively reinforce the public narrative that Wario himself was dead. It was a dual-purpose propaganda strike broadcast across the Midland's emergency frequencies.

Bowser and Hjumpik, sitting in a dark cave having just lost a friend, listened to this recording in its entirety. 

They had no context for Wario's sophisticated misinformation campaigns. They heard the voice of the Mushroom Kingdom's greatest hero confessing to being an irredeemable monster. They looked at the radio, looked at each other, and formed a devastatingly logical, entirely incorrect conclusion: Mario was evil, the Mushroom Kingdom was corrupt to its core, and everything they knew was a lie.

This false paradigm shift would color their interactions with the world for months to come.

## Section IX:


The Wrong Blimp to Swiftsoul

Fuelled by disgust at the voicemail and the trauma of the caves, Bowser and Hjumpik finally battered their way to the surface. They emerged blinking into the smoky, soot-stained daylight, expecting to see the borders of the Mushroom Kingdom.

They had exited on the completely wrong side of the continent.

Bowser's navigational intuition had failed them with a precision that bordered on the mathematical. They were stranded in a barren, rocky valley. In the distance, a massive commercial transport blimp was hovering low, taking on emergency refugees fleeing the dragon crisis.

Having no other options, Bowser and Hjumpik flagged it down and boarded. 

Bowser immediately demanded to know when they would arrive at the Mushroom Kingdom. The terrified pilot informed the massive, blood-stained Koopa that this blimp was heading strictly north, ascending into the high mountain peaks toward the military aerodrome of Swiftsoul Keep.

Bowser was furious. The blimp was heading in the exact opposite direction of his intended destination. He spent the entire multi-day journey pacing the gondola, complaining loudly about the altitude, the lack of legroom, the incompetence of Midland cartography, and the fundamental injustice of a universe that kept moving his kingdom further away from him. Hjumpik sat in silence, anchoring the duo's sanity as the blimp slowly ascended into the freezing clouds.

Meanwhile, miles away on the ground, Archie Miser, the pirates, and Markop (who had temporarily abandoned his pursuit of his father after losing the trail in the ash) arrived at the misty gates of Ravencreek, entirely unaware that a God Toad was hunting them, a fake dragon was waiting in an arena, and their eventual extraction vehicle would be stolen in a hail of gunfire. 

The convergence of Disaster Inc. was moving into its final, inevitable phase.

WAH.
